title: IdP compatibility & SSO edge-case integration guide (Okta/Azure/Google/Ping)
creator: Avery Chen
description: Deliver an IdP-specific compatibility and runbook docset for SSO/SAML integrations covering Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, and Ping. The scope includes: mapping IdP SAML attributes to RBAC v2 (role & group claims), documenting attribute transformation rules and recommended IdP settings, enumerating known edge cases and fallback behaviors, defining audit log events and required fields, and authoring step-by-step admin controls + troubleshooting guide to ship with Console and Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: A single consolidated doc (Confluence) exists that lists tested IdP configurations and the exact attribute mappings we support for RBAC v2
Integration test matrix updated: for each IdP, positive/negative cases for group-to-role mapping, SCIM sync (where applicable), and SAML NameID formats are verified
Console admin UI shows the expected human-readable error messages for common IdP misconfigurations (mismatched audience, missing role claim, expired cert)
Audit logs include standardized fields for SSO events (event_type, user_id, idp, saml_request_id, saml_response_status, mapping_result) and a migration note for existing logs
Engineering PR with the runtime fixes and config parsers merged and a follow-up release note added to security-2026.04
tasks: Run IdP compatibility tests against Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, Ping (SAML flows + SCIM where applicable)
Document exact attribute names we accept (e.g., groups, roles, app_metadata) and provide recommended transform rules for each IdP
Add telemetry hooks for SAML failure reasons; ensure errors are human-readable in Console and included in audit events
Create troubleshooting section for admins: certificate rotation, clock skew, audience/recipient mismatch, NameID-format issues
Author quick-start config snippets for each IdP and upload to docs.redwood.ai SSO guide
Coordinate with PM/Docs to link the guide from onboarding and the Console SSO setup flow

notes: Key deliverable is an operational guide that the Support and Solutions Engineering teams can follow when customers report SSO failures. Emphasize deterministic behavior: when multiple acceptable claim names exist, our normalization rules should be listed and justified. Include a short migration guide for existing customers moving to RBAC v2 so admins can map old role enums to new role objects.
observations: Okta: standard, but many tenants use custom app attribute mappings. Recommend adding example Groovy/Expression mappings for the common patterns.
Azure AD: inconsistent use of 'roles' vs 'groups' depending on Enterprise App settings; requires explicit app manifest configuration for group claims >2000 users.
Google Workspace: often requires custom SAML attribute mapping; SCIM support limited to Google Cloud Identity customers.
Ping: supports rich transforms but customer docs often omit the expected SAML settings; include Ping-specific certificate rotation steps.
